title: Scheduled Backup Encryption Misidentified as Ransomware
description: A file server triggered a mass-file-modification alert during an overnight backup job. Files were written into encrypted backup containers, but there were no ransom notes, no user-access failures, and the job matched an approved backup schedule.
raw_logs: 2026-07-01T23:02:00Z siem rule=Mass_File_Modification host=FILE-SRV-03 process=backupagent.exe files_modified=1204 interval_seconds=60
2026-07-01T23:02:07Z edr host=FILE-SRV-03 process=backupagent.exe signer=Approved_Backup_Systems signature=valid verdict=clean
alert_source: SIEM, File Audit, EDR, Change Management
remediation: Close as benign after confirming the signed backup agent, expected schedule, backup destination, and absence of ransomware indicators. Consider tuning the mass-file-modification rule with an approved backup-process exception.
analyst_notes: High file-write volume and encryption can resemble ransomware, but the approved signed backup process, known schedule, expected backup path, and lack of ransom-note or access-loss indicators support a benign explanation.
expected_answer: This should be classified as benign rather than ransomware. The model should identify the key contextual evidence, avoid mapping to T1486, assign low severity, and recommend safe detection tuning rather than incident containment.
missing_evidence: Historical baseline for backup write volume
